files.purpose: MCPStore is the @MainActor @Observable model owning every MCP server connection the user has made: it stores per-catalog-id connection records and live connection states, holds in-progress field drafts for the connect/edit cards, and owns the list of user-defined custom servers. It is the single place that turns a connect/disconnect/refresh/setEnabled/saveCustom/saveCustomValues action into a persisted MCPConnection (plus Keychain secrets), a background probe Task tracked in `probes`, and a full re-export of every provider's config file (MCPProviderConfig, MCPExternalSync) and the in-process MCPHub/MCPProxy routing, so the rest of the app (Settings UI, chat providers) never talks to the catalog or the filesystem directly.
state_owned: probes: [String: Task<Void, Never>] (not persisted, in-memory only)
side_effects: Reads/writes MCPPaths.connectionsURL and MCPPaths.customsURL as JSON (atomic writes)
Reads/writes secret field values in the Keychain via MCPKeychain
Starts/cancels background probe Tasks per catalog id
Registers/unregisters routes on MCPProxy.shared and rewrites every provider's on-disk config on every mutating call via exportAll()
Triggers an MCPHub.shared.reload() Task on every export
platform_assumptions: Swift structured concurrency (Task, Task.checkCancellation(), CancellationError) for the cancellable per-server probe, which the port models with an explicit TaskHandle/cancellation-token abstraction (R-TASK-1) rather than raw Swift Task semantics
@MainActor/@Observable for SwiftUI observation of connections/states/drafts/customs, matched on the C# side by a MainActorModel base with Read/Computed wrappers

JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder with .iso8601 date strategy and .sortedKeys/.prettyPrinted output formatting for the two persisted files, and Swift's Dictionary/String ordinal comparison semantics for `.sorted { $0.id < $1.id }` (must use an ordinal, not culture-aware, string comparer on Windows)
persisted_fields: MCPPaths.connectionsURL: JSON array of MCPConnection (catalogID, isEnabled, values, connectedAt, serverVersion, tools), sorted by catalogID, iso8601 dates
MCPPaths.customsURL: JSON array of MCPCustomServer definitions
Keychain: one secret entry per (server id, field key) for fields of kind .secret
ui_elements: No direct UI in this file; it is the backing model for the MCP settings/connect cards (MCPSetupPanel/MCPKeyPanel per the B2->B3 diff of DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/) which read `drafts`, `states`, `connections`, and call `connect`/`disconnect`/`refresh`/`setEnabled`/custom-server editing through this store
feature_notes: The only B2->B3 change in this file is the removal of the `allEntries` computed property (old lines 51-56: two doc-comment lines, `var allEntries: [MCPCatalogEntry] { customs.map { $0.catalogEntry() } + MCPCatalog.entries }`, and its trailing blank line) — a clean 6-line deletion with no other edits anywhere else in the file, confirmed by `git diff 1fbf81e61e28a079508a074c01ee1830a9cc23dc HEAD -- DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift` showing exactly one hunk `@@ -48,12 +48,6 @@`.

`allEntries` was dead code even in B2: `grep -rn allEntries` across the whole B2 tree (E:\Droppyeference\droppy-code-v1.6.2) finds only its own declaration in this file, no caller anywhere in the app (Settings views enumerate the catalog and customs some other way). The B3 commit message (d70cff8fe, 'refactor: audit cleanups — five bug fixes, shared MCP and provider code, layer rules restored') and its very large multi-file diffstat confirm this was part of a deliberate dead-code/audit cleanup pass across the whole MCP and Providers area, not a behavior change to any live feature.

Because exactly 6 lines were removed at old line 51, every symbol at or after old line 57 shifts by a uniform -6 in B3 (spot-checked: storedValues old 293-301 -> new 287-295 at B3:287; disconnect old 120-134 -> new 114-128 at B3:114; the final catch old 350-353 -> new 344-347 at B3:344-347); nothing at or before old line 50 (state(for:), enabledServers, init, drafts, `16 drafts`, `22-28 init()`, `26-28 init's start-then-export order`) moved at all.

The removed property is still present in the Windows port: E:\Droppy\wt\integration\src\Marrow.Services\MCP\MCPStore.cs:69-71 defines `public IReadOnlyList<MCPCatalogEntry> AllEntries => Computed(() => Customs.Select(...).Concat(MCPCatalog.Entries).ToList());` citing B2 lines :51-55, and it is likewise unreferenced anywhere else under src/ (grep for `AllEntries` across E:\Droppy\wt\integration\src finds only this one declaration) — so removing it changes no observable port behavior, only conformance to the pinned source.
